1. About Astera

Astera is a private foundation on a mission to steer science and technology toward a better future. We believe the coming years will bring an era of unprecedented scientific and technological advancement as exponential progress in AI converges with central advances in other fields to accelerate innovation. This inflection point provides an unparalleled opportunity to fundamentally rethink the institutions, systems, and tools that drive progress. We have committed a $3.5B endowment to that work and fit the form of our support to the function it serves: grants, investments, and in-house research programs. We accept meaningful risk in the research we back and expect some of it to fail because transformative ideas are rarely the ones already proven. Our projects, and the foundation itself, operate like high-velocity startups, with a high performance bar and competitive compensation to match. We are searching for leaders who are compelled by the challenge of driving high-impact change in the way science is funded, conducted, and communicated. You can read more about our mission, vision, and programming at astera.org/vision http://astera.org/vision.



2. Company Overview

Astera Neuro seeks to understand and engineer consciousness. We believe consciousness is the process by which the brain builds a coherent internal model of the world and the self. We aim to understand this model and to develop the technologies to write experience directly into the brain. By combining large-scale neural recording, causal perturbation, and brain-based AI, we seek to move neuroscience from observing correlates of experience to engineering it. The same tools carry direct therapeutic promise for neurological and psychiatric diseases that alter perception, thought, and sense of self. Because the science and tools required do not yet exist, we are assembling a founding team of neuroscientists, theorists, and engineers to create them. We do high-risk, high-reward science in a well-resourced, collaborative environment with competitive pay, and share everything openly under Astera’s Open Science Policy.



3. Position Summary

We are hiring a scientist to join Astera Neuro’s experimental neuroscience team and develop the viral and molecular tools the research program runs on. Your primary responsibility will be to develop and screen AAV-based tools for neural imaging and optogenetic manipulation, including new combinations of genetically encoded indicators and opsins, and new strategies for achieving efficient, specific, and reliable expression. These tools support all-optical experiments in mice and nonhuman primates (NHPs).



Reliable expression is a rate-limiting step for the experiments we intend to run, so the tools you build set the ceiling on what the rest of the program can attempt.



The ideal candidate pairs strong molecular biology with hands-on rodent or NHP surgery. You can design and generate a construct in the morning, perform stereotaxic injections in the afternoon, and quantify expression on the two-photon rig that evening. Animal wellbeing is foundational to this work, supported by dedicated veterinary and behavioral care staff and rigorous welfare standards.



We are hiring at multiple levels. As a Research Associate, you will run established molecular and screening workflows with regular guidance. As a Senior Research Associate, you will own the screening pipeline end to end and drive construct design decisions. As a Scientist, you will set the viral and transgenic expression strategy for the program, mentor research associates and technicians, and shape how tools work is planned with the experimental teams. We will calibrate scope and title to your experience.



4. What You’ll Do

 1.  Develop and screen AAV-based tools for neural imaging and optogenetic manipulation, including new indicator and opsin combinations and strategies for improving expression efficiency, specificity, and reliability.

 2.  Design, generate, and validate molecular constructs using cloning, plasmid preparation, sequence verification, and related molecular biology techniques.

 3.  Run the viral screening pipeline end to end in mice and NHPs, coordinating AAV production with external vendors and quantifying expression brightness, sparsity, titer dependence, volume dependence, and success rate.

 4.  Quantify expression in vivo using one-photon and two-photon imaging, including z-stacks, to establish whether co-expression resolves in single cells and whether a construct meets the requirements of downstream all-optical experiments.

 5.  Perform or support survival surgery in mice and NHPs: stereotaxic viral injection, chronic cranial-window implantation, and headbar installation.

 6.  Validate genetic tools in vitro and in vivo using fluorescence microscopy, tissue processing, and histology.

 7.  Support transgenic mouse breeding, genotyping, and genetic strategies for targeted expression.

 8.  Work closely with neuroscientists and engineers to integrate new genetic tools into imaging and optogenetic experiments.

 9.  Keep careful, shared records of constructs, viral preparations, screening results, surgeries, and protocols so others can build on the work.

 10. Contribute to publications, talks, open data and tooling releases, and engagement with the broader scientific community.



5. Who You Are

a. Required

 1. BS, MS, or PhD with 0 to 8+ years of experience in molecular biology, neuroscience, genetics, bioengineering, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience. We value demonstrated skill and relevant experience above credentials.

 2. Strong hands-on experience with molecular cloning, DNA construct design, and standard molecular biology techniques.

 3. Experience with viral-vector-based gene delivery, particularly AAV systems.

 4. Demonstrated hands-on experience performing stereotaxic viral injections in mice or NHPs.

 5. Hands-on experience with tissue processing, histology, and fluorescence microscopy.

 6. Ability to execute and troubleshoot molecular biology and animal experiments independently, while holding a high standard of experimental quality and reproducibility.

 7. Strong organizational skills and careful record-keeping.



b. Preferred/Nice to Have

 1. Chronic cranial-window implantation or related surgical preparations in NHPs.

 2. Chronic cranial-window implantation in mice.

 3. Developing or screening genetically encoded calcium or voltage indicators, optogenetic actuators, or related tools.

 4. Developing high-throughput assays for screening viral constructs or genetic tools.

 5. Transgenic mouse breeding, genotyping, and colony management.

 6. Immunohistochemistry.



6. What We Value

 1. Conviction that the brain’s internal model can be understood in full, and that getting there requires a kind of science no single academic lab can do; we are betting on scale, deep collaboration across science and engineering, and open sharing of ideas in a full-stack environment.

 2. Willingness to be held to an engineering standard. In this role that standard lands on the tools: we treat expression reliability and screening yield as scientific results, not support work.

 3. Comfort building on shared infrastructure rather than private projects; constructs, viral preparations, and screening records are standardized so they can be shared across the team.

 4. Care for the animals: healthy, well-handled animals, supported by dedicated veterinary oversight, are the foundation of both the science and its credibility, independent of what regulation requires.

 5. Commitment to open science. We release tools, data, and methods, and aim to create a new dynamic of rapid, open exchange in neuroscience.



7. Compensation

The posted salary range is based on location in the Bay Area. The successful candidate will receive a competitive compensation package, commensurate with their experience and location.



8. Why Join Us

Astera Neuro is hiring a scientist to build the viral and molecular tools that all-optical neuroscience depends on: the constructs, screens, and expression strategies that decide what the rest of the program can attempt in mice and NHPs. This work sits within Astera Neuro’s larger effort to answer the hardest and least understood questions in neuroscience: how the brain generates thoughts, intelligence, and consciousness.



Astera Neuro provides a comprehensive benefits package and total compensation that is competitive and commensurate with the level of experience and qualifications.



We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity and inclusion!
